To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can perform an end-to- end sound source separation (with a variable number of sound sources) using a deep learning approach, and that we can improve the separation results by using multiplicative conditioning with the instrument labels at the WaveU- Net bottleneck.

(1) we present a novel end-to-end SSS approach with a variable number (up to 4) of sources, (2) we propose an approach to use instrument labels for conditioning, and (3) we show that this conditioning improves the separation results.
We extend WaveU-Net to perform monaural source separations with a variable number (1 to 4) of sources and show its effect by comparing the separation results with the original WaveU-Net.

the proposed method is a step forward in end-to-end sound separation with a non-deterministic number of sources.
our model is a promising approach for end-to-end SSS conditioned on instrument labels.
the proposed approach can be applied to any kind of SSS problem where the number of sources is known and the sources can be conditioned upon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show the potential of the WaveU-net architecture for end-to-end SSS and the effectiveness of conditioning with labels at the bottleneck.
we have extended the Wave-U-net model to allow end-to-end separation of an arbitrary number of sources and have also shown the effect of instrument labels conditioning on the separation performance.
we propose the first end-to-end model for SSS conditioned on instrument labels and we also show how this model can be used for audio-visual source separation and score-informed separation

the proposed method is able to perform SSS conditioned on the number of sources.
